question: Which part in the ovule helps in guiding the pollen tube (carrying sperm nuclei) towards the female gamete?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Synergids**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Synergids** are two specialized cells located at the **micropylar end** of the **embryo sac** in **angiosperms**. They are part of the **egg apparatus**, which also includes the **egg cell** (female gamete).
 
• The primary function of **synergids** is to guide the **pollen tube** toward the female gamete. This guidance is achieved through **chemotropic attraction**, where the synergids secrete specific chemical substances that direct the pollen tube's growth.
 
• Inside the synergids, there is a specialized cellular structure called the **filiform apparatus**. These are thick, finger-like projections of the cell wall that play a vital role in directing the **pollen tube** into the **embryo sac** and facilitating the release of **sperm nuclei**.
 
• During the process of fertilization, one of the **synergids** usually starts to degenerate before or upon the entry of the **pollen tube**, creating a passage for the male gametes to reach the egg cell and the central cell. ***Hence, the statement that synergids help in guiding the pollen tube is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Antipodal Cells**:
 
 
• These are a group of **three cells** located at the **chalazal end** (opposite to the micropyle) of the **embryo sac**.
 
• In most plants, their function is to provide **nutrition** to the developing **embryo sac**, although they typically degenerate before or shortly after **fertilization**.
 
 
 
• **Endosperm**:
 
 
• The **endosperm** is the nutritive tissue formed as a result of **triple fusion** (one male gamete fusing with **two polar nuclei**) during **double fertilization**.
 
• It is usually **triploid (3n)** and serves as a food source for the **embryo** during **seed development** and germination.
 
 
 
• **Style**:
 
 
• The **style** is the long, slender tube-like part of the **carpel** (or pistil) that connects the **stigma** to the **ovary**.
 
• While the **pollen tube** must grow through the tissues of the **style** to reach the **ovule**, the **style** itself does not provide the final chemical guidance into the **embryo sac**; that role belongs to the **synergids**.
 
 
 
• **Double Fertilization**:
 
 
• This is a characteristic feature of **flowering plants** (angiosperms) where **two male gametes** are released into the **embryo sac**.
 
• One male gamete fuses with the **egg cell** to form a **diploid zygote (2n)**, and the other fuses with the **central cell** containing **two polar nuclei** to form the **primary endosperm nucleus (PEN)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **embryo sac** in a typical angiosperm is an **8-nucleate, 7-celled** structure.
 
• The **micropyle** is the small opening in the **integuments** of the **ovule** through which the **pollen tube** usually enters.
 
• The **chemotropic signals** involved in guidance often include **calcium ions** and specific **proteins** secreted by the **filiform apparatus**.
</ul
